narrativeReportMd:
# Expression R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
`Expression` keeps the same identity and local element set, but it has one clear local R4-to-R6 validation break: `Expression.name` changed from the primitive `id` type to `code` and gained the `exp-2` variable-name pattern. R6 also makes `Expression.language` optional, which is a R6-to-R4 conversion gap, and changes the expression-language value set from an HL7-specific CodeSystem to selected BCP-13 media-type codes.

## Scope
The analysis covered the R4 and R6 core StructureDefinitions, package indexes and metadata, the expression-language value sets, the R4 expression-language CodeSystem, the mimetypes value set, and the primitive `id`/`code` definitions used to understand the `name` type change. Inherited `Element`/`DataType`/`Extension` behavior and the R4 `Element` to R6 `DataType` base-definition shift are out of scope for this artifact report.

## Main migration themes
The main migration issue is stricter naming: R4 names such as `risk-score`, `query.1`, or `1query` can satisfy the R4 `id` primitive but fail the R6 variable-name invariant. The second theme is cross-version conversion: R6 can omit `language`, but R4 requires it. The third theme is terminology realignment for `language`, where the old `application/x-fhir-query` code is no longer in the R6 expression-language value set and R6 introduces `text/x-fhir-query`, `text/cql-identifier`, and `text/cql-expression`.

## Highest-impact findings
The highest-impact finding is `Expression.name` because it can make previously valid R4 fragments fail R6 validation and can affect generated model types and validation code. The terminology finding is less deterministic because the binding remains extensible, but it is important for validators, enum-like bindings, and systems that dispatch expression engines based on exact `language` codes.

## Findings requiring human review
The expression-language terminology change deserves human review because no local ConceptMap or authoritative BCP-13 expansion was available. Implementers should confirm whether legacy `application/x-fhir-query` should be transformed to `text/x-fhir-query` in their migration context.

## Backward-compatible design observations
The `name` constraint appears aimed at making expression names usable as variables in common languages, but it could have been introduced less disruptively as a warning, profile constraint, or new normalized-name element. Making `language` optional is backward-compatible for R4-to-R6 validation but deliberately sacrifices lossless R6-to-R4 conversion for authoring-only expressions.

## Follow-up analysis
Base datatype inheritance should be reviewed in the `DataType`/`Element` reports. Terminology owners or migration tooling should review the expression-language value set and any cross-version mapping for query and CQL sublanguage codes.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `Expression` has one hard local R4-to-R6 break in `Expression.name`, plus R6-to-R4 and terminology migration risks around `Expression.language`. The biggest practical concerns are renaming old `id`-style names that are not valid R6 variable names, deciding how to backfill missing R6 `language` values for R4 targets, and mapping expression-language codes. Confidence is high for StructureDefinition deltas and medium for terminology intent because no official diff or ConceptMap was available.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should validate all `Expression.name` values against the R6 `exp-2` pattern and decide whether to rename invalid values, preserve them in extensions, or reject affected records. R6-to-R4 conversion needs a policy for expressions without `language`. Terminology migration should treat exact language-code matching as version-sensitive, especially for FHIR query expressions.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high that the local element, cardinality, type, and invariant changes were identified because both R4 and R6 StructureDefinitions were present and directly matched by canonical URL. Confidence is lower for terminology business impact because the value sets are unexpanded locally and no official mapping from the R4 HL7 expression-language CodeSystem to the R6 BCP-13 codes was found.

findings.title: Expression.name changed from id to code and gained a variable-name invariant

oldState.summary: Optional name with primitive type id and no local Expression-specific name pattern.

semanticText.short: Short name assigned to expression for reuse
semanticText.definition: A short name assigned to the expression to allow for multiple reuse of the expression in the context where it is defined.

oldState.narrativeMd: In R4, `Expression.name` was an `id`. The R4 `id` primitive allows letters, digits, hyphen, and dot up to 64 characters, so values such as `risk-score`, `query.1`, or `1query` could be structurally valid.

newState.summary: Optional name with primitive type code and local exp-2 invariant requiring a common-language variable name.

constraints.human: The name must be a valid variable name in most computer languages

semanticText.short: Short name assigned to expression for reuse
semanticText.definition: A short name assigned to the expression to allow for multiple reuse of the expression in the context where it is defined.

newState.narrativeMd: In R6, `Expression.name` is a `code` and is subject to `exp-2`: it must start with a letter and then contain only letters, digits, or underscore, with a maximum length of 64 characters.

facts.note: The wire-level JSON member name stays `name`, but primitive validation and generated model typing can change.
The invariant is new in R6 and is referenced from `Expression.name`.

facts.field: R6 Expression.name accepted pattern after exp-2

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The element path and id remain `Expression.name`; this is not a rename. The material change is the local type and validation domain.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct R4-to-R6 validation break for any R4 instance whose `name` uses an `id` form that is not a valid R6 variable name, such as a hyphen, dot, or leading digit. Runtime risk is high for strict validators, generated primitive wrapper types, and code that uses `Expression.name` as a map key or symbolic identifier. R6-to-R4 risk also exists because R6 permits underscore in names, while the R4 `id` primitive does not.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The change is primarily technical and conformance-oriented. Clinical or business risk would arise indirectly if expressions cannot be located or executed after a failed migration.

justification.inferredGoal: Make expression names usable as variable identifiers in common expression and programming languages.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain the R4 `name` shape and add advisory or profile-level variable-name guidance, or add a separate variable-safe alias.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred R6 goal is reasonable: an expression name used for reuse is more interoperable when it is a valid variable identifier in common languages. The break is probably justified because a base-level guarantee requires rejecting dashed, dotted, or digit-leading R4 names. However, the local evidence does not include an official change rationale, and less-breaking designs could have preserved existing data with weaker guarantees.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have kept `Expression.name` as the R4 `id`-shaped value and introduced the variable-name rule as a warning, best-practice invariant, or profile requirement. Another option would be an optional variable-safe alias while retaining the original `name`. These are only partial alternatives: advisory/profile enforcement would mean base R6 consumers could not rely on every `name` being variable-safe, while an alias design risks indefinite duplicate representations of the same reusable name.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves legacy names, but either weakens the base R6 guarantee or creates parallel original and normalized names that consumers must reconcile.

evidence.detail: The R4 `id` primitive regex allows letters, digits, hyphen, and dot.
R6 adds an error invariant requiring `name` to match a variable-name pattern.

examples.examplesMd: These are datatype fragments, not complete resources. `risk-score` illustrates an R4 `id` value that fails R6 `exp-2`; `risk_score` illustrates an R6-valid variable-style name that is not valid under the R4 `id` primitive.

findings.narrativeMd: `Expression.name` is the only local element with a clear hard R4-to-R6 instance-validation break. The path did not move or rename, but the allowed value space changed. Existing expressions that used dotted, dashed, or digit-leading names can fail R6 validation even though they were legal R4 `id` values.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4-valid fragment with `name: "risk-score"` can become R6-invalid because `exp-2` rejects the hyphen. This affects strict validation, generated model primitives, and any code that assumes names can be copied without normalization. In the reverse direction, an R6 `name` containing underscore can be valid in R6 but not valid as an R4 `id`, so R6-to-R4 conversion may require lossy renaming or an extension to preserve the original.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Scan all `Expression.name` values before migration. For values that do not match `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,63}`, choose a deterministic normalization rule, preserve the original value in an extension or side table if references depend on it, and update any local references that use the old name. Test hyphenated, dotted, digit-leading, underscore, maximum-length, and absent-name cases.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change is understandable if R6 wants reusable names to behave like variables, but a base-level error invariant was not the only possible design. A warning invariant or profile-specific rule would have allowed old R4 data to remain base-valid while nudging new implementations toward variable-safe names. The tradeoff is that consumers could no longer rely on every base R6 `Expression.name` being variable-safe.

findings.title: Expression.language minimum cardinality decreased from 1 to 0

binding.description: The media type of the expression language.

oldState.narrativeMd: In R4, every `Expression` had to carry `language`, even if the expression was only a reference or was not executable.

binding.description: The media type of the expression language.

semanticText.requirements: The cardinality of this element is optional to allow text only as part of the authoring process.  However, in order to be executable, the expression element must be specified.

newState.narrativeMd: In R6, `language` can be omitted. The new requirements text says this supports authoring-only text, while executable expressions still need a specified language.

facts.newValue: The cardinality of this element is optional to allow text only as part of the authoring process. However, in order to be executable, the expression element must be specified.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The same element id and path are present in both versions; only the minimum cardinality and explanatory requirements text changed.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is not a hard R4-to-R6 break because R4 instances that include `language` still satisfy the R6 cardinality. It is a R6-to-R4 representability risk: a base-valid R6 `Expression` can omit `language`, but R4 requires it. Runtime risk appears when R4-generated code or expression dispatch logic reads R6 data and assumes a non-null language.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The primary risk is failed conversion or inability to execute an expression, not a direct clinical safety issue.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow non-executable or authoring-time expression text without forcing a language code.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable for R4-to-R6 compatibility: decreasing `language` from 1..1 to 0..1 preserves R4-valid instances in base R6.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 requirements text gives a concrete goal: permit text-only authoring states while still expecting a language for executable expressions. Because this is a cardinality weakening, it is not a breaking R4-to-R6 base-design issue. The remaining concern is reverse conversion to R4, so the R6 design is probably justified even though migrations need an explicit policy for missing language.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No less-breaking R4-to-R6 base alternative is needed because every R4 instance that supplied the required `language` remains valid against the R6 minimum cardinality. A stricter R6 design could have kept `language` required, used a sentinel value, or relied on an extension/profile for authoring-only expressions, but those are round-trip or modeling alternatives rather than backward-compatible alternatives to an R4-to-R6 break.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Optional `language` supports authoring-only text but creates an R6-to-R4 conversion gap; keeping it required would force artificial or misleading language values.

evidence.detail: R6 explains that optional cardinality supports text-only authoring, but executable expressions require a language.
evidence.quote: The cardinality of this element is optional to allow text only as part of the authoring process.

r6NotRepresentableInR4Json.description: Authoring-time expression text whose language is not yet declared

migrationExampleJson.description: Authoring-time expression text whose language is not yet declared

examples.examplesMd: The first fragment is R6 base-valid because `language` is optional and `expression` satisfies `exp-1`; it is not R4-valid because R4 requires `language`. The migration example only works if the missing language can be safely inferred.

findings.narrativeMd: `Expression.language` is no longer mandatory in R6. This is a widening change for R4-to-R6 validation, but it matters for round-trip conversion and runtime code because many R4 implementations will have generated `language` as required and may use it to select the FHIRPath, CQL, or query engine.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: No R4-valid instance becomes invalid merely because of this cardinality change. The compatibility issue is the reverse: an R6 instance without `language` cannot be represented as a valid R4 `Expression` without inventing, inferring, or otherwise supplying a language code. A parser may accept the fragment structurally, but R4 validation should fail the missing required element.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R6-to-R4 transforms, detect missing `language` and avoid blindly defaulting. If the language can be inferred from context, add it and document the rule. If it cannot be inferred, preserve the R6 content in an extension or reject/quarantine the record for manual review. Tests should cover omitted language with `expression`, omitted language with `reference`, and executable expressions where language is still expected by business logic.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change is forward-compatible but not round-trip-compatible. Keeping `language` required would have maximized R4 compatibility, but it would have forced authoring-only content to supply a possibly misleading language. The R6 choice appears justified if supporting non-executable authoring states was more important than lossless conversion to R4.

findings.title: Expression.language value set changed from HL7 expression-language codes to selected BCP-13 media-type codes

oldState.summary: Extensible binding to expression-language value set composed from the R4 HL7 expression-language CodeSystem.

binding.description: The media type of the expression language.

changedCodes.newMeaning: Clinical Quality Language as a BCP-13 media-type code.
changedCodes.changeSummary: The code string remains `text/cql`, but the value set source system changes in R6.

changedCodes.newMeaning: FHIRPath as a BCP-13 media-type code.
changedCodes.changeSummary: The code string remains `text/fhirpath`, but the value set source system changes in R6.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The R4 value set included all concepts from `http://hl7.org/fhir/expression-language`; the local R4 CodeSystem listed `text/cql`, `text/fhirpath`, and `application/x-fhir-query`.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 used an HL7-defined expression-language CodeSystem with three complete concepts. The FHIR query language code was `application/x-fhir-query`.

newState.summary: Extensible binding to the same canonical value set, but the value set now enumerates selected BCP-13 media-type codes and adds a maximum binding to mimetypes.

binding.description: The media type of the expression language.

changedCodes.oldMeaning: FHIR query was represented in R4 as `application/x-fhir-query` in the HL7 expression-language CodeSystem.
changedCodes.newMeaning: FHIR query is represented in R6 as `text/x-fhir-query` in BCP-13.
changedCodes.changeSummary: FHIR query language code and code system changed.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: R6 `ValueSet/expression-language` is immutable and includes selected concepts from `urn:ietf:bcp:13`: `text/cql`, `text/fhirpath`, `text/x-fhir-query`, `text/cql-identifier`, and `text/cql-expression`.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 keeps the binding strength and value set canonical URL, but the value set composition changes materially. It now enumerates BCP-13 media-type codes and adds an additional maximum binding to `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/mimetypes`.

facts.note: The canonical is unchanged, but the value set definition behind that canonical changes.
R4 represented this as an extension; R6 represents it as `binding.additional` with purpose `maximum`.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The affected element and binding canonical are the same; the material change is in the bound value set composition and expression-language code inventory.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The binding remains extensible, so this is not the same as a required-binding code removal. However, extensible bindings still carry a conformance obligation to use value-set codes when they apply. R4 instances using `application/x-fhir-query` may be flagged or require mapping in R6, while R6 instances using `text/x-fhir-query`, `text/cql-identifier`, or `text/cql-expression` are not cleanly representable as R4 expression-language codes. Runtime dispatch based on exact language codes or generated enums can break even when structural validation accepts the primitive code.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The likely business risk is expression-engine misrouting or failed conformance validation, especially for query and CQL library-reference use cases.

justification.inferredGoal: Align `Expression.language` with real media-type identifiers and distinguish CQL identifiers from inline CQL expressions.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep legacy `application/x-fhir-query` in the R6 expression-language value set as a deprecated alias while adding the BCP-13 replacement and CQL-specific codes.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal is reasonable: align expression languages with media-type identifiers and distinguish CQL identifiers from inline expressions. A deprecated legacy alias could have reduced disruption for R4 query expressions, but it would have undercut the clean terminology transition and preserved two codes for the same operational concept. Given the extensible binding and lack of a local ConceptMap, the change is probably justified but not fully demonstrated by the supplied evidence.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would include both `application/x-fhir-query` and `text/x-fhir-query` in the R6 value set for a transition period, mark the old code deprecated, and publish a ConceptMap. This is a partial alternative because it preserves common R4 query instances but introduces duplicate same-element representations, validation ambiguity for the preferred code, and ongoing burden for validators and expression-engine dispatch tables.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Would reduce migration friction, but leaves duplicate codes for the same query language and may require exact-code dispatch support indefinitely.

evidence.detail: R4 `Expression.language` has an extensible binding to `ValueSet/expression-language` and a maxValueSet extension pointing at BCP-13.
R4 `ValueSet/expression-language` includes all concepts from the HL7 expression-language CodeSystem.
R6 represents the maximum binding as an additional binding to `ValueSet/mimetypes`.

examples.examplesMd: `application/x-fhir-query` was the R4 expression-language code for FHIR query. R6 uses `text/x-fhir-query`. Because the binding is extensible, these examples illustrate conformance and runtime dispatch risk rather than guaranteed JSON-schema rejection in every validator.

findings.narrativeMd: `Expression.language` keeps the same binding strength and canonical value set URL, but the value set contents change substantially. The R4 HL7 CodeSystem is replaced by selected BCP-13 media-type codes, including a changed FHIR query code and new CQL-specific codes. Systems that treat language as an enum or exact dispatch key need explicit cross-version mapping.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: A strict terminology-aware validator may flag old `application/x-fhir-query` in R6 because the corresponding R6 value-set code is `text/x-fhir-query`; because the binding is extensible, behavior may vary by validator and terminology server. Conversely, R6 codes such as `text/cql-identifier` are not present in the R4 expression-language CodeSystem, so lossless R6-to-R4 representation needs a ConceptMap, extension, or local convention.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Create an explicit language-code mapping table. At minimum, review whether `application/x-fhir-query` should map to `text/x-fhir-query`, and decide how R6 `text/cql-identifier` and `text/cql-expression` should be represented in R4. Update validators, generated enum bindings, expression-engine dispatch tables, and test fixtures for old query code, new query code, and the added CQL codes.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The terminology change is probably justified by media-type alignment, but it could have been less disruptive if R6 retained the old query code as a deprecated alias or supplied a ConceptMap in the core package. That alternative would ease migration at the cost of allowing two codes for the same operational concept.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Human review is recommended because no authoritative terminology expansion or ConceptMap was present locally, and the R6 value set uses the external `urn:ietf:bcp:13` code system.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: The canonical URL, id, name, kind, type, derivation, and abstract flag match. Status and standards-status changed but are reported as non-breaking; the base-definition shift is out of scope as a base datatype hierarchy issue.

The local R4 elements `description`, `name`, `language`, `expression`, and `reference` are all present with the same paths in R6. No local additions, removals, renames, moves, splits, or merges were found.
`Expression` has no local `Reference`-typed element in either version.
No local `Expression` element is marked as a modifier in either version.
The local summary flags remain stable: `description`, `name`, `language`, `expression`, and `reference` are summary elements in both versions.
No local `Expression`-owned slicing was found. Slicing on inherited `extension` is out of scope.
No local fixed value, pattern value, or default value constraints were found on `Expression` elements.

No local maxLength, minValue, maxValue, fixed, or pattern constraint was found. The material lexical-domain change for `Expression.name` is reported as a type/invariant finding rather than a primitive value-limit finding.

`exp-1` still requires either `expression` or `reference`; R6 adds `source` metadata and condition annotations to affected elements. The new local `exp-2` invariant is reported as a material finding. Inherited `ele-1` and `ext-1` behavior is out of scope.

Definitions and shorts are mostly stable. R6 adds requirements text explaining optional `language` and adds a comment clarifying that `expression` may name content within a referenced expression; these are noted as migration-awareness items, not separate hard breaks.

No JSON/XML element names or local element paths changed. Serialization/code-generation risk is limited to the reported primitive type and validation-domain change for `Expression.name` and requiredness assumptions for `Expression.language`.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Expression maturity/status advanced from draft trial-use to active normative
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The computable status and standards-status metadata changed, but this does not by itself invalidate instances or change the serialized content model.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Treat R6 `Expression` as a more stable/normative datatype, but do not interpret the maturity change as a data transform requirement.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 clarifies how expression and reference can be used together
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R6 adds a comment that if both `Expression.expression` and `Expression.reference` are present, `Expression.expression` might be a name pointing within the referenced content. This does not alter cardinality, type, or the existing `exp-1` rule.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Implementers that previously assumed `expression` always contained the full executable text should review combined `expression` plus `reference` handling, but existing data is not structurally invalidated by this clarification.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds explicit condition annotations for existing Expression constraints
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R6 annotates `Expression.expression` and `Expression.reference` with condition `exp-1`, and `Expression.name` with condition `exp-2`. The `exp-1` rule itself is unchanged; `exp-2` is reported separately as a material finding.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Code generators or documentation tools may show the constraints closer to the affected elements in R6, but this is mostly metadata presentation except for the new `exp-2` rule.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: R6 `Expression` derives from `DataType` whereas R4 derives directly from `Element`. Per scope instructions this class-hierarchy change should be owned by the `DataType`/base-artifact assessment, but it may affect generated inheritance trees for all datatypes.

`Expression.language` depends on the changed expression-language value set. A terminology-specific review should confirm intended mappings and deprecations, especially for `application/x-fhir-query` to `text/x-fhir-query`.
R6 expression-language codes are selected from the external BCP-13 media-type system, which was not locally available as a complete CodeSystem resource.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No official R4-to-R6 diff, Jira issue, or change note was supplied. Justification and backward-compatible alternative analysis are inferred from the computable definitions and embedded comments.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: A standards change log or Jira ticket explaining the intended migration behavior for `Expression.name` and `Expression.language`.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Terminology impact was assessed from local ValueSet and CodeSystem composition, not from live expansions or terminology-server validation. This matters because the `Expression.language` binding is extensible and R6 uses external BCP-13 media-type codes.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Authoritative expansions for the R4 and R6 value sets plus a ConceptMap or migration note for legacy expression-language codes.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The local core package does not indicate how common non-variable-safe `Expression.name` values or FHIR query language expressions are in real implementations.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: A corpus scan of real R4 artifacts, IGs, and production examples containing `Expression` values.

Bindings whose canonical value set URL is stable but compose systems/codes changed
R6 optional elements that were required in R4 and affect R6-to-R4 transforms
